firestore.reasoning:
Given the requirement for admin access managed via Firebase Custom Claims (which will not be used) and the application's focus on an agent directory, the data structure prioritizes storing user and agent data in separate collections. The structure is designed to allow for straightforward security rules and efficient data retrieval.  Because Custom Claims are not stored in the database, Authorization Independence does not need to be implemented here. QAPs are addressed via role existence checks, as well.

Since we will not be using Custom Claims as per the instructions, a database-centric role assignment can be implemented.

/roles_admin/{userId}: This collection is used to grant admin roles. The existence of a document with the user's ID in this collection grants admin privileges. Rules will be simple: only admins (themselves) can create their own documents; only admins can list this collection.

/users/{userId}: Stores user profile data.  This collection allows users to manage their profile data. Rules: Users can only manage their own documents; admins can read any user document.

/agents/{agentId}: Stores the agent data.  This is a flat collection containing all agents.  Rules will allow read access to everyone, and creation/modification restricted to admins.  The 'verified' boolean field allows for filtering agents based on their verification status. This supports a QAP because admins can verify agents.
